findings.reason: without a declared attribution rule the census is a worker choice rather than a measured quantity, so the node's central figure is unreproducible and its comparison across a re-run means nothing.
findings.text: the census asks for a value's signals "split by deciding source ... the five figures for each value summing to 1,766", but the section names three sources and never says which single bucket a signal belongs to when two of them agree (the pilot's 190 signal-list-linked signals are exactly the population where the archive's unit and the linked row's unit are most likely to agree); the sum forces one bucket per signal while the rule that picks it is unstated, so two correct readings produce different five-figure tables that both sum to 1,766 and the figure cannot fail on attribution

findings.reason: the node must either fail an absolute done-when clause or silently resolve the disagreement the same line forbids resolving, so the two halves of the gate contradict each other and one of them needs the conflict carve-out written in.
findings.text: "Where a signal already carries a unit from the archive or the controls metadata, the assigned unit equals it for every such signal" is unqualified, while the negative control on the same line requires "a signal whose sources disagree on the unit" to be recorded as a conflict; for a signal whose archived unit and controls-metadata unit differ the assigned unit cannot equal both, so the equality clause is unsatisfiable exactly for the population the conflict state exists to hold, and the census expects conflicts to exist
